title: 2021 ESC Guidelines on Cardiovascular Disease Prevention in Clinical Practice

definitions.Secondary Prevention: Prevention of recurrent CV events in individuals with established CVD
definitions.SCORE2: 10-year risk of fatal and non-fatal CV events in adults 40–69 without prior CVD or DM
definitions.Polypill: Fixed-dose combination tablet containing aspirin, statin, and antihypertensive
definitions.Healthy Life Years: Combines survival and quality of life into one measure

recommendations.text: SCORE2/SCORE2-OP risk estimation is recommended in all adults ≥40 years without established CVD or DM for primary prevention decision-making.
All adults should be advised that not smoking is the single most effective lifestyle measure for CV prevention.
A Mediterranean diet (high in vegetables, legumes, fruit, fish, olive oil; low in red meat) is recommended for primary CV prevention.
Regular moderate-intensity aerobic exercise (≥150–300 min/week) is recommended for prevention of CVD.
Body weight management targeting BMI 20–25 kg/m² and waist circumference <94 cm (men) / <80 cm (women) is recommended.
Statins are recommended for primary prevention in high and very-high-risk patients who do not reach LDL-C goals with lifestyle changes.
Antihypertensive drug treatment is recommended in adults with Grade 2–3 hypertension or Grade 1 with high/very-high CV risk.
Aspirin for primary prevention is not recommended in persons at low or moderate cardiovascular risk.
Aspirin is recommended for secondary prevention in all patients with established ASCVD.
GLP-1 receptor agonists are recommended in patients with type 2 diabetes at high/very-high CV risk to reduce CV events and mortality.
SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended in patients with type 2 diabetes at high/very-high CV risk to reduce CV events, HF hospitalization, and mortality.
Measurement of carotid intima-media thickness or coronary artery calcium (CAC) score may be considered for refinement of risk stratification.
Cardioprotective agents should be initiated (statin + antihypertensive) in cancer patients receiving cardiotoxic therapies at high CV risk.

lifestyle_targets.diet: Mediterranean; reduce processed food, red meat, trans fats, added sugar
lifestyle_targets.physical_activity: 150–300 min/week moderate or 75–150 min/week vigorous aerobic; 2x/week muscle-strengthening
lifestyle_targets.alcohol: ≤100 g/week (men and women); no safe level — abstinence preferable

pharmacotherapy.indication: Primary prevention at high/very-high risk; all secondary prevention

pharmacotherapy.examples: semaglutide 0.5–1 mg SC weekly, liraglutide 1.2–1.8 mg SC daily
empagliflozin 10–25 mg, canagliflozin 100–300 mg, dapagliflozin 10 mg

pharmacotherapy.indication: Secondary prevention (Class I); NOT for primary prevention (Class III)

key_trials.name: ASPREE
key_trials.finding: No CV benefit; increased bleeding and cancer mortality in elderly

key_trials.name: LEADER
key_trials.finding: 13% RRR in CV death, MI, stroke in T2DM with CVD

key_trials.name: SUSTAIN-6
key_trials.finding: 26% RRR in MACE in T2DM with high CV risk

key_trials.name: EMPA-REG OUTCOME
key_trials.finding: 14% RRR in MACE; 35% HF hospitalization reduction; 32% renal progression

key_trials.name: CANVAS
key_trials.finding: 14% RRR in MACE; 33% HF hospitalization reduction

key_trials.name: DAPA-CKD
key_trials.finding: 39% RRR in composite renal/CV outcome in CKD
